description: Width tiers for Design and Technologies Year 9-10 band (ACARA v9). All 11 descriptors. Generated from elaborations using width_generation_prompt v1.0.
subject: Design and Technologies

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest honest engagement that satisfies the descriptor's command term. For K strand (analyse and make judgements): minimum contexts or phenomena that demonstrate genuine analysis, not just identification. For P strand (capability): narrowest task context in which the process skill is applied with evidence of independent execution.
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope as ACARA intends it. Grounded in the most common elaboration cases. For K strand: the range of phenomena, contexts and systems the descriptor is intended to cover. For P strand: the full range of process phases the capability encompasses.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add phenomena, contexts or application domains. For K strand: additional phenomena or cases that extend the analytical framework. For P strand: additional task contexts, complexity levels or real-world application scenarios. First Nations contexts included where elaborations indicate them.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations are source data, not a checklist. Typical_width is grounded in common elaboration cases. Wider may reasonably extend beyond elaborations where the direction is clearly within the descriptor's scope and year band.

AC9TDE10K01.minimum_width: Analyse how at least one design and technologies occupation integrates ethical, security and sustainability factors — explaining what the occupation considers and how it shapes design decisions; explain what product life cycle thinking is and give one example of its influence.
AC9TDE10K01.typical_width: Analyse how people in design and technologies occupations consider ethical, security and sustainability factors — including product life cycle thinking, ethics in mass production (labour, supply chain, product versions), professional contributions to societal problems, and the consequences of ethical and sustainability decisions for users and environments; examine at least one example of professional global collaboration.
wider: Investigate the sustainable production of culturally significant First Nations pigments (e.g. calcination process) as an example of life cycle thinking embedded in traditional practice
Analyse the Cao Lanh Bridge collaboration between Australian and Vietnamese engineers — identify each party's contribution and what made the collaboration necessary
Examine design decisions for public infrastructure that reduce fire risk in rural communities — evaluate the ethical, sustainability and safety considerations balanced in the design
Analyse mass production systems for food, clothing or footwear — evaluate the ethics and sustainability of each stage and the different product versions that result
elaborations: examining sustainability factors influencing the design and production of a solution developed by First Nations Australians, such as the sustainable production of culturally significant pigments
analysing design and technologies professions and their contributions to society, for example engineers working in disaster recovery or empowering communities
recognising the impact of past designed solutions when creating solutions for preferred futures
considering the factors that influence design and manufacture and the work of professional designers including time, access to skills, knowledge, finance, expertise in global engineering
explaining how product life cycle thinking can influence decision-making related to design and technologies
examining mass production systems taking into account ethics and sustainability considerations
explaining the consequences of ethical and sustainability decisions for products, services and environments

AC9TDE10K02.minimum_width: Describe one example of innovation driven by emerging technology and its impact on a designed solution; apply one future-thinking technique (forecasting or backcasting) to a scenario and identify one implication.
AC9TDE10K02.typical_width: Analyse how innovation, enterprise and emerging technologies interact to create designed solutions for preferred futures — including how commercial enterprises respond to technological change, how diverse knowledge systems (including First Nations) contribute to innovation, and how forecasting and backcasting techniques reveal opportunities and impacts for society.
wider: Research how spinifex grass biodegradable polymers draw on First Nations knowledge — analyse what knowledge was the foundation and what contemporary research extended it
Apply backcasting to a specific global challenge (food security, clean energy) — identify the design and technology decisions required at each stage toward a preferred future
Compare how two enterprises in the same sector responded differently to the same technological shift — analyse why their responses differed and which was more effective
Investigate intellectual property frameworks for First Nations knowledge in design — identify what protections exist and where gaps remain
elaborations: investigating how the knowledges of First Nations Australians have led to the discovery of potential innovative solutions, for example biodegradable polymers using spinifex grass
exploring the ways commercial enterprises respond to the challenges and opportunities of technological change, for example e-commerce, and considering their carbon footprint
investigating scenarios of how the future may unfold and what opportunities and impacts there may be for society using forecasting and backcasting techniques
examining real-world problems and understanding basic needs when considering designed solutions, for example students collaborating to design solutions to challenges in the Asia region

AC9TDE10K03.minimum_width: Explain how material properties combine with force, motion and energy in one engineered system; calculate at least one force or load in a simple structure.
AC9TDE10K03.typical_width: Analyse and make judgements on how material characteristics and properties combine with force, motion and energy to control engineered systems — including calculating forces, reactions and loads in structures; critiquing the effectiveness of specific system combinations (e.g. vehicle safety, 3D printers, wind turbines); and explaining why combinations of properties, not single properties, determine system performance.
wider: Investigate the engineering of First Nations Australian spearthrowers — analyse how material properties (rigidity, flexibility, hardness) are exploited and the biomechanical advantage achieved
Analyse vehicle safety features (seatbelts, airbags, crumple zones) as a system — explain how each element controls force transfer and why the combination is more effective than any single feature
Investigate wind farm turbine placement to maximise productivity within a given space — analyse the force and energy relationships that determine optimal layout
Investigate EV charger types and capabilities — apply quantitative reasoning to make a recommendation for a specific use case
elaborations: investigating the engineering innovations of First Nations Australians, such as spearthrowers and bow and arrow, and how characteristics and properties of materials are used
explaining the way common machines or engineered systems interact and combine properties of materials, force, motion and energy efficiently
calculating forces, reactions and loads in structures and analysing the relationship between materials of properties, forces and safety in engineered systems such as bridges
critiquing the effectiveness of the combinations of materials, forces, energy and motion in an engineered system such as a 3D printer
investigating how the placement of wind turbines in a wind farm affects their performance
investigating the main types of chargers for electric vehicles and their capabilities

AC9TDE10K04.minimum_width: Analyse at least one emerging production technology for productivity, sustainability and ethical implications; explain one environmental interdependency in a food or fibre production system; describe at least two stages in a marketing chain and explain how processing or advertising affects price or demand.
AC9TDE10K04.typical_width: Analyse and make judgements on the ethical, secure and sustainable production and marketing of food and fibre enterprises — including emerging production technologies (protected cropping, hydroponics, aquaculture, precision agriculture), environmental interdependencies, food and water security implications, and the marketing chain from production through to consumer.
wider: Analyse First Nations Australian grain sources (e.g. acacia) for nutrient content and suitability as sustainable food sources in drought-prone regions — compare with conventional cereal crops
Investigate digital production tools (GPS, crop sensors, automated feeding, drones for weed management) and evaluate how they change the ethics and sustainability profile of production
Trace the full marketing chain of a global agricultural commodity (e.g. coffee, cotton, cacao) — make judgements on where ethical trade practices are and aren't present
Investigate the impact of a cash crop economy on a specific community — analyse how dependence on a single export crop affects food security and economic resilience
elaborations: analysing grain sources used by First Nations Australians, such as acacia, for their nutrient content and suitability as a sustainable food source
examining emerging production technologies and methods in terms of productivity, profitability and sustainability, including animal welfare considerations
investigating how digital tools could be used to enhance food production systems
investigating the interdependence of plants and animals and comparing the environmental impacts of intensive and extensive production systems
considering the meaning of food and water security and how they may influence design decisions
examining the marketing chain of a range of agricultural products and outlining the effect of product processing and advertising on demand and price

AC9TDE10K05.minimum_width: Describe at least two sensory characteristics and explain how they affect a food design decision; explain one food preservation method and how it changes the food's properties; identify one food trend and its influence on healthy eating design.
AC9TDE10K05.typical_width: Analyse and make judgements on how sensory and functional food properties influence sustainable food solution design — including sensory and nutritional assessment, food preservation methods (freezing, dehydrating), safe food handling and danger-zone temperatures, and current food trends (plant-based, organic, non-dairy); evaluate how different properties and trends shape design choices for healthy eating.
wider: Analyse how First Nations Australians' detoxification techniques (e.g. cycad nuts) reflect sophisticated knowledge of the functional properties of food — compare with contemporary food processing approaches

Evaluate competing food trends (e.g. plant-based protein vs conventional, non-dairy vs dairy) using nutritional and environmental evidence — make a judgement on which better serves a sustainable healthy eating solution
Investigate emerging food technologies (3D food printing, IoT food supply chain, AR food labelling) — evaluate the potential benefits and risks for healthy eating design

Design a healthy canteen item using a current food trend — document how sensory, nutritional and sustainability criteria shaped the design; use food photography and digital promotion tools to communicate it
elaborations: analysing how First Nations Australians have long understood techniques to turn plant products into food sources with high nutritional value
experimenting with food preservation methods such as freezing and dehydrating to determine changes to food structure
conducting sensory and nutritional assessment testing of a range of foods to determine how these characteristics might be used to enhance food solutions
determining how the causes of food spoilage can be addressed when preparing, cooking, presenting and storing food items
reflecting on food trends and how they may influence choosing food or designing food solutions for healthy eating
investigating ways innovations may influence human health and sustainability, for example 3D printing of foods, Internet of Things (IoT) in the food supply chain
considering factors that influence the preparation and presentation of foods using a range of techniques to ensure optimum nutrient content, flavour, texture and visual appeal

AC9TDE10K06.minimum_width: Identify at least one environmental consequence of material selection in an existing product and describe one sustainable alternative; describe one emerging material and explain how it changes a design possibility.
AC9TDE10K06.typical_width: Analyse and make judgements on how characteristics and properties of materials, systems, components, tools and equipment can be combined to create designed solutions — including critiquing environmental consequences of material selection, investigating emerging materials (bioplastics, nanomaterials, medical textiles), and justifying selection decisions from a broad technology range with reference to sustainability, weight, safety, cost and performance requirements.
wider: Analyse First Nations Australians' use of possum fur for thermal clothing — examine how material properties (insulation, biodegradability) are exploited and how this knowledge is applied in contemporary high-performance thermal clothing
Critique common plastic bag design and evaluate sustainable alternatives (bioplastics, seaweed-based materials) — make a judgement on which best balances performance, cost and environmental benefit
Investigate soft robotics nanomaterials that function like human muscles — evaluate what design possibilities this opens and what engineering challenges remain
Investigate fibre-based medical textiles (e.g. collagen fibre sutures) — analyse how the combination of properties creates solutions conventional materials cannot achieve
Justify selection of locally sourced materials (e.g. bamboo CLT) for a specific structural application — evaluate carbon footprint, performance and cost against a conventional alternative
elaborations: analysing how First Nations Australians identified the superior thermal properties of possum fur in developing products such as cloaks including making judgements on how these fibres are sourced
critiquing the design of an existing product to identify environmental consequences of material selection and investigating emerging materials such as bioplastics or seaweed
justifying decisions when selecting from a broad range of technologies — tools, equipment, processes, materials, systems and components
analysing and explaining the ways in which the properties and characteristics of materials have been considered in the design of a product with specific requirements
investigating emerging materials and their impact on design decisions, for example bioplastic material made from discarded potato peels
investigating fibre-based medical textile products and structures used in a medical environment
investigating soft robotics including nanomaterials which enable them to function like human muscles

AC9TDE10P01.minimum_width: Analyse a need or design opportunity for a specific context; write a design brief with a problem definition, at least two user needs, and at least one constraint; investigate and select at least one material, component or tool with a justification.
AC9TDE10P01.typical_width: Analyse needs or design opportunities by investigating users, contexts and constraints; independently develop a design brief incorporating user needs, sustainability, ethical considerations, and accessibility or Safety by Design principles; investigate and select materials, systems, components, tools and equipment with justified selection decisions.
wider: Analyse First Nations Australians' traditional grains for commercial and nutritional potential — develop a design opportunity statement that responds to this as a brief starting point
Interview community members about accessibility requirements to identify an unmet design need — document what the interviews revealed that desk research would not have found
Develop a design brief that explicitly addresses Indigenous cultural and intellectual property rights — explain what considerations this adds
Research a specialist emerging material and evaluate whether it is appropriate for the design project — justify the decision with reference to properties, availability, cost and sustainability
elaborations: analysing First Nations Australians' traditional grains for their potential for providing nutritional and commercial solutions
analysing the design of new products to identify how well design ideas respond to sustainability issues
developing design briefs that take into consideration the needs of users, for example universal design principles or Safety by Design principles
analysing a range of design and technologies ideas including those that draw on the intellectual property of others, including Indigenous cultural and intellectual property rights
considering the needs of community groups to identify rich design tasks, for example interviewing community members about accessibility requirements
examining tools, techniques, equipment and relationships of properties for complementary materials

AC9TDE10P02.minimum_width: Generate at least two distinct design concepts using an ideation technique; analyse one design idea against at least two of functional, structural and aesthetic dimensions; produce at least one drawing or model; document one design decision with a justification.
AC9TDE10P02.typical_width: Apply innovation and enterprise skills to generate, test, iterate and communicate design ideas — including analysis of functional, structural and aesthetic benefits and constraints for different communities and environments; production of technical drawings, digital models and/or physical prototypes; and clear documentation with appropriate technical language and justified decisions for an intended audience.
wider: Use nature-inspired design (biomimicry) as an ideation framework — generate concepts that translate a natural mechanism into a designed solution
Analyse a design for suitability in an earthquake zone (e.g. Japanese skyscraper design) — explain how structural and functional requirements differ from standard contexts
Produce multiple prototypes exploring competing aesthetic considerations — explain how each prioritises different factors and what user feedback would inform the choice
Develop a design communication package for an enterprise context — pitch the design concept to a target market audience rather than a technical audience
Use 3D printing or AR modelling to prototype a design — explain what this representation reveals that 2D drawing cannot
elaborations: using techniques including combining and modifying ideas and exploring functionality to generate solution concepts and reimagining designs to feature emerging technologies
undertaking functional, structural and aesthetic analysis of benefits and constraints of design ideas, for example assessing how a design is suitable for different communities and environments
considering competing variables that may hinder or enhance project development
producing drawings, models and prototypes to explore design ideas, for example using technical drawing techniques, 3D printers or augmented reality modelling software
communicating using appropriate technical terms and recording the generation and development of design ideas and processes
using design thinking and enterprise skills to create innovative approaches to processes and solutions

AC9TDE10P03.minimum_width: Set up and use at least one tool or piece of equipment independently with appropriate safe working practices; experiment with at least two approaches to a material or technique and evaluate the results; identify and respond to at least one production risk or unforeseen challenge.
AC9TDE10P03.typical_width: Select, justify, test and use suitable technologies, skills and processes with independence and appropriate safety procedures — including independent equipment setup with PPE, experimentation with material combinations documented and evaluated with peers, sustainability-conscious material choices, and adaptation of production processes in response to unexpected challenges.
wider: Independently set up a specific machine (e.g. lathe) to produce a part to specified dimensions — explain each setup step and its safety rationale
Experiment with food prepared three ways to maximise colour, flavour and nutritive value — evaluate which best meets the design criteria
Document a production adaptation made in response to an unforeseen challenge — evaluate whether it maintained quality and what you would do differently
Investigate how bulk food production introduces coordination and scaling challenges — experiment with adapting a recipe for bulk production and evaluate quality and safety outcomes
Experiment with an innovative material combination not previously used together — document findings collaboratively and evaluate against design requirements with peers
elaborations: refining technical skills and using production skills with independence to produce quality designed solutions
using materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques safely and considering alternatives to maximise sustainability
experimenting with innovative combinations and ways of manipulating traditional and contemporary materials and recording findings in a collaborative space
modifying production processes to respond to opportunities, risks or unforeseen challenges
experimenting with the functional and sensory properties of food to determine the most successful approach

AC9TDE10P04.minimum_width: Independently write at least two assessable design criteria including at least one sustainability criterion; evaluate at least one design or technology choice against criteria; reflect on at least one process choice and explain what would be done differently.
AC9TDE10P04.typical_width: Independently develop design criteria including sustainability to evaluate design ideas, processes and solutions — including specific, assessable criteria covering function, aesthetics, safety and sustainability; justified evaluation of technology choices (traditional, contemporary, emerging) against criteria; reflection on process choices at multiple stages; and iteration in response to evaluation feedback.
wider: Develop criteria with measurable performance thresholds (e.g. acceptable load, stress test result) — explain how you would verify whether the solution meets each criterion
Develop criteria that address the full product life cycle, not just the use phase — including sourcing, production and end-of-life criteria
Evaluate whether a technology choice that is superior on performance criteria is inferior on sustainability criteria — make and justify a final decision
Document a full iteration cycle — what evaluation feedback prompted the change, what was modified, and whether the change improved the solution against the criteria
elaborations: establishing specific design criteria for evaluating designed solutions, for example determining necessary function of a product and making a judgement about whether these have been met after stress testing or user testing
evaluating and justifying the use and best combination of traditional, contemporary and emerging technologies during project development, including consideration of sustainability
reflecting on learning including processes or choices made at various stages of a design process and modifying plans when needed with consideration of design criteria
responding creatively to evaluation feedback to iterate and modify design ideas and processes to improve sustainability measures

AC9TDE10P05.minimum_width: Produce a production timeline using a digital tool with at least three sequenced tasks and one dependency; assign roles and tasks to team members with at least one contingency; identify at least one production enhancement strategy.
AC9TDE10P05.typical_width: Develop project plans for intended purposes and audiences that manage time, cost, risk, processes and production — including production timelines and flowcharts using digital tools, equitable collaborative role distribution with contingencies, and investigation of manufacturing strategies to enhance production through waste reduction, cost reduction or beneficial partnerships.
wider: Create a production flowchart that maps all decision points including safety checks, quality reviews and sustainability decisions
Produce a materials and equipment needs analysis using a spreadsheet — calculate quantities, costs and sourcing requirements
Investigate lean manufacturing principles — identify which apply to the design project and explain how they would change the production plan
Map production waste at each stage and identify reduction strategies — evaluate the sustainability benefit of each
Develop a contingency plan addressing at least three distinct risks — test the contingency by simulating a specific risk event and evaluating the response
elaborations: producing, explaining and interpreting drawings and planning production timelines using digital tools, for example establishing materials and equipment needs using spreadsheets, or creating production flowcharts
collaborating to develop production plans for equitable distribution of work including discussing roles, tasks and deadlines and considering flexibility and contingencies
investigating manufacturing processes to identify strategies to enhance production, for example identifying techniques to reduce use, cut costs, speed up processes or to form beneficial partnerships
